evidence.excerpt: This paper investigates the degree to which near-field emission maps acquired with a planar probe array can predict far-field radiated emissions measured at a 3 m open-area test site (OATS). Forty-eight printed circuit board assemblies representing five product categories were characterised using a custom 64-element magnetic probe array with 5 mm probe pitch at heights of 3 mm and 8 mm above the board surface. Near-field data were processed with an equivalent dipole model to extrapolate far-field values. The mean absolute error between predicted and measured peak emissions was 4.2 dB, with 90 % of predictions falling within ±7 dB of OATS reference measurements in the 30–300 MHz range. Accuracy degraded above 500 MHz, where near-field spatial aliasing became significant at the chosen probe pitch. The method reduced test preparation time by approximately 60 % compared to full OATS campaigns in an iterative design cycle. Limitations related to enclosure shielding effects and cable routing variability are discussed.
